segments._note: WAS a `wall` (height 0.95) — a near-vertical riser that read as a TELEPORT up. Converted to a short STAIRCASE of the SAME total height so the climb is visibly STEPPED (2 treads, riser 0.475u over 1.2u run each). LENGTH-GATE preserved: overall slope 0.396 < steepThresh 0.6 ⇒ NOT hook-gated (a normal length-gated staircase); each riser 0.475u > maxClimb(0.6)=0.30 ⇒ a SHORT leg (reach ~0.6) is BLOCKED at the foot (struggle-in-place, no soft-lock), a LONG leg climbs it tread-by-tread. So a too-short leg is still blocked SOMEWHERE (NO-SINGLE-LEG holds) but there is NO vertical snap.

STEEP CLIMB = hook-gated STAIRCASE, ~50deg (overall slope 4.4/3.7=1.189 >= 0.6 => auto hook-gate). Matches the reference: TALL step edges (each step rise 0.88u > its run 0.74u) are the grip points. HEIGHT kept at 4.4 (course vertical profile preserved); the steeper angle comes from a SHORTER run, not a taller top. Only a HOOK leg grips & climbs; straight/round legs slip => struggle-in-place at the foot => redraw a hook to pass (no soft-lock). Reach-irrelevant. 5 steps over 3.7u => each 0.74u run / 0.88u rise (clearly stepped grip points, not micro-serrations).

PHYSICS BALL PILE — a heap of dynamic spheres the cube must SHOVE aside. Plowing through slows the cube (resistance ∝ contacts, floored ⇒ no soft-lock); the balls roll/scatter ahead. Pure additive obstacle (no gate).
GAPPED PLANKS — long/fast leg (big stride) sails over the voids; short leg drops into the shallow recovery trench and crawls out (slow, no soft-lock). Long-favourable.

BREAKING BLOCKS — a low wall of upright boxes barring the path. blockH 0.8 is JUST UNDER the cube (CUBE_SIZE 0.9) so the cube clearly SITS ON / rides OVER the blocks and the rubble (NOT buried among taller towers — was 1.4, which sank the cube). The cube SMASHES each on contact: the block bursts into debris that falls, litters the floor, and SLOWS the cube grinding over the rubble (resistance ∝ contacts, floored ⇒ no soft-lock). The cube always breaks through, riding on top. Reuses the ball-debris physics (gravity/clamp/separation/cube-push).

The SPLIT-PATH FORK that USED to sit between the preceding flat(4) and these bumps was REMOVED from the course (it read as a confusing split). The fork ENGINE code is kept (track_schema `fork` kind, walker fork build/_commitForkAt/forkLateralAt, renderer _buildForks) so it can be re-added later. The flat(4) ends at baseY=0 and these bumps start at baseY=0 (sin starts at 0, whole periods) => the join is continuous, NO discontinuity. finishX recomputed 331.5 -> 319.5 (removed the fork's 12u arc-length; the 35u run-out buffer past the last content is preserved).

STRAIGHT RUN — the winding 'curve' (도는 길) S-bend that USED to sit here was REMOVED per user request (the rotating/spiral road felt forced). The two `curve` segments (turn +65/-65 over 44u) were deleted and replaced by this single straight flat so the course stays coherent and the road no longer rotates. finishX recomputed 319.5 -> 275.5 (removed the 44u of curve arc-length; everything after shifts left 44u). The `curve` ENGINE code (track_schema `curve` kind, walker heading/yaw, renderer curving path) is KEPT dormant so a straight road is unaffected and curves could be re-added later. Lead-in flat(6) merged with the old flat(4) after the curves into flat(10).

WAS a `wall` (height 1.0). Converted to a 2-step STAIRCASE of the SAME total height (riser 0.5u over 1.3u run each). slope 0.385 < 0.6 ⇒ length-gated (NOT hook-gated); riser 0.5u > maxClimb(0.6)=0.30 ⇒ short leg BLOCKED, long leg climbs stepped. No vertical snap.

WAS a `wall` (height 0.95). Converted to a 2-step STAIRCASE of the SAME total height (riser 0.475u over 1.2u run each). slope 0.396 < 0.6 ⇒ length-gated (NOT hook-gated); riser 0.475u > maxClimb(0.6)=0.30 ⇒ short leg BLOCKED, long leg climbs stepped. No vertical snap.
